description: Query-family performance baseline, measured nightly on a GitHub-hosted runner against a generated, non-personal dataset.
establishmentNote: STILL DELIBERATELY UNSET, and — unlike the build-size, container, coverage and schema baselines, which run 19 established — this one could not be filled in by this initiative. scripts/db/perf-baseline.mjs has only ever run against a developer machine, and those numbers say nothing about a shared 2-vCPU hosted runner. The measurement belongs to the `performance-baseline` job in nightly-assurance.yml, and that workflow has never executed: a `schedule:` trigger only fires from the repository's DEFAULT branch, and this workflow exists solely on feature/platform-comprehensive-ci-automation. The GitHub Actions API confirms it — across the repository's entire run history the only workflows that have ever run are `CI`, `PR CI` and `P1-21 Hosted Clean Room`, and nightly appears zero times.
whenThisGetsEstablished: The first nightly run after this branch merges into develop. Nothing further is required: the job already writes the measurement, and `queries` stays empty until a human commits it. No PR-gate job reads this file, so an unset performance baseline cannot block the pipeline — nightly-summary.mjs classifies `performance-baseline` as `informational` precisely so that a missing budget reports as missing rather than as passing.
budgetRationale: p95 rather than p50, because a regression that only moves the median is usually noise and one that moves the tail is usually real. ×1.5 is wide on purpose: a shared CI runner is a noisy instrument, and a budget that cries wolf gets ignored, which is worse than no budget.
noiseFloorRationale: Below about 5 ms the ratio is arithmetic about jitter. A query going from 1 ms to 2 ms is ×2 and means nothing.
absoluteChecksFromDayOne: A sequential scan on a tenant-leading indexed lookup fails immediately, with no baseline needed — that is a missing or unusable index, not a slow machine.
An empty measurement set fails. Nothing measured must never read as fast.
